clue.text: Rude gesture? Then it's time to abandon a game

parts.note: to cock a snook is to put thumb to nose with fingers spread, a rude gesture

indicators.note: time is told to abandon the word a, so that letter drops out of the period

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone makes a rude gesture and decides it is time to walk away from a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon a' takes A from ERA, leaving ER. The question mark makes 'Rude gesture?' look like a whole sentence, but it only supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue sport played on a baize table, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Domestic servant, awfully hideous, mum retained

indicators.note: the mother is kept inside the jumbled letters, as a servant is kept on
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of hideous are jumbled

parts.note: mum and ma are both familiar words for mother

explanation.surface: A complaint about a maid who is horribly unpleasant while the mother keeps her on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the letters of the word hideous, and 'retained' keeps the mother's word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemaid is a female servant employed to clean a house, a kind of domestic servant.

clue.text: Wear nothing, needing to get into shelter

indicators.note: the zero has to get into the shelter, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter or refuge
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with no clothes on needs to dive into cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a garment on is to be wearing it, an idiomatic synonym for wear.

clue.text: Separate area reached by sailors

indicators.note: the area is reached by the sailors, who arrive first and so come before it

parts.note: AB is able-bodied seaman, so ABS are sailors
a tract is an expanse or area of land

explanation.surface: A remote region that only seamen can get to.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to remove or separate it from a larger whole, as a verb.

clue.text: Victorian artist when drunk could be bleary dauber, yes?

indicators.note: being drunk leaves things in disorder, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was the Victorian artist, when tipsy, a bleary-eyed slapdash painter? Yes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges BLEARY DAUBER YES into the artist's name. Aubrey Beardsley was an English illustrator of the 1890s known for black-ink drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrey Beardsley was an English illustrator active in the 1890s, an artist of the late Victorian period.

clue.text: It's safe to go outside home for a picnic

indicators.note: the safe word goes outside the word for home, wrapping round it

parts.note: secure means safe, protected from harm
in means at home

explanation.surface: Is it secure to leave the house for an outdoor meal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a picnic' is used in its sense of something easy, not an outdoor meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post needing little work, and an easy task is colloquially a picnic.

clue.text: Engineers appropriate for providing a new set of equipment

definitions.text: providing a new set of equipment
definitions.note: the definition reads as a gerund naming an act, matching the noun sense of re-equipping

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: Military engineers are the right people to kit out a unit again.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is the overhaul and re-equipping of a ship or building with new fittings.

clue.text: A mark the French waiter is given

definitions.text: A mark the French waiter is given

parts.words: A mark the French waiter is given
parts.note: the French word for waiter carries a small hook under its C, the mark meant here, not a score or tip

explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the diacritic hook under a C in French words such as the word for waiter.

clue.text: Country making a new attempt when backed by the French

indicators.note: the French article stands behind the rest, so it comes last

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A nation tries again with French support.
explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a country in south-west Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: What knocks back editor — if a VIP is genuine

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the other way, so the run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a nob is a person of wealth or standing, a VIP

explanation.surface: Something that rebuffs the editor, if a dignitary is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks back' turns the whole run ED IF A NOB backwards. 'What' and 'is' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for in good faith, used in English to mean real or authentic.

clue.text: Title of my French gentleman used around European community

parts.note: mon is the French word for my

indicators.note: the gentleman's word is used around the community, wrapping it

parts.note: sir is the form of address for a gentleman
EU is the European Union, a community of European states

explanation.surface: A French form of address for a man, used across the European community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' is the definition; 'of' is a joining word, and 'used around' puts the community's letters inside the gentleman's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur is the French courtesy title for a man, the equivalent of Mr.

clue.text: Moggie let out with other animals

parts.note: moggie is British slang for a cat, usually an ordinary pet one

indicators.note: out suggests something gone wrong or disordered, so the letters of let are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet cat is let out to join other creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into TLE. 'other animals' is a fair definition because a moggie is itself an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are cows, bulls and oxen, a group of farm animals other than the cat.

clue.text: Mayor with yen to move in a particular social group

indicators.note: the letters are made to move into a new order

explanation.surface: A mayor with a yearning to mix in a certain level of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges MAYOR YEN. 'yen' is a longing, not the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were the class of small landowning farmers, a distinct social group in English history.

clue.text: London complex issuing claim of competence following insult

indicators.note: the claim comes after, following the insult

parts.note: a barb is a cutting, insulting remark
saying I can is a claim to be capable of something

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of their ability after being insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbican is a large arts and residential complex in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbican is a large estate and arts centre in London, a complex of buildings.

clue.text: Tiny rec in derelict downtown area

indicators.note: derelict means run down and ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A small recreation ground in a run-down part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derelict' rearranges TINY REC IN. A rec is a recreation ground, a public park or playing field in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner city is the central, often deprived, district of a town, its downtown area.

clue.text: One arguing about a member of the family starts to exaggerate ridiculously

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a member of the family

indicators.note: only the starting letters of the two following words are taken

explanation.surface: A family quarrel where someone wildly overstates their case.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoner is a person who argues logically, someone who presents arguments.

clue.text: Plant Zola and I found in meadow

parts.note: Zola Budd was a South African-born distance runner who raced for Britain in the 1980s

indicators.note: the letter is found in the meadow, inside it

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow

explanation.surface: A plant that Zola and the speaker came across in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola points to the runner Zola Budd, not the French novelist Emile Zola.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering shrub often called the butterfly bush, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Straighten out nut that's drunk alcoholic drink

indicators.note: a drunk nut is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Telling a drunken crackpot to sort himself out with some booze.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to untwist something tangled, so to straighten it out.

clue.text: Ramble with ungrammatical alternative to 'The Queen and I'?

indicators.note: the phrase is rephrased with the wrong pronoun case and the order swapped, as careless speakers do

parts.note: me is the object form of I, used ungrammatically as a subject
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on a common slip in speaking about oneself with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Queen and I' said badly is 'me and her', and ER stands in for her.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, like a winding river, so it means to ramble.

clue.text: Happy, having existed again with inner energy

indicators.note: the energy is placed inner, within the other word

parts.note: relived means lived again, existed once more
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Feeling good after a second life with fresh vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means freed from worry, so glad and happy that a fear has passed.

clue.text: See restricted literature — a particular novel

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
lit is a shortened form of literature, the word cut down

explanation.surface: A banned book that readers are warned about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' suggests censorship, apt for this controversial novel, but it only shortens literature to LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Vladimir Nabokov's 1955 novel, a specific and once controversial book.

clue.text: Things collected from street in the morning — empty pots

parts.note: AM means before noon, in the morning

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone gathering discarded empty pots from the street early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage stamps are things philatelists collect, so they are a classic collected item.

clue.text: Swot showing face at university

parts.note: mug is slang for face
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A studious student's face is seen around campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Swot is British slang for studying hard, here a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for studying a subject hard, which is also to swot.

clue.text: So fortifying and comforting

parts.note: taken as written
lacing a drink is fortifying it with spirits

explanation.surface: A warming drink both strengthening and soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Solacing means consoling, giving solace, which is to be comforting.

clue.text: Pure music comes from this

definitions.meaning: pure in the sense of chaste or untouched
an early keyboard instrument like a small harpsichord, popular in the 16th and 17th centuries

explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means chaste or untouched, and the virginal was a small Tudor keyboard instrument producing music.

clue.text: Sit back collecting the sums of money for the church?

definitions.text: sums of money for the church?

indicators.note: the reversed word gathers the next word inside it
the word sit is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sitting back while the church collection plate goes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns sit round, giving TIS, and 'collecting' wraps it round the word the; 'for the church?' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithes were a tenth of produce or income paid to support the church and clergy.

clue.text: American movement that's presided over by mad character?

definitions.meaning: a conservative US political movement that arose around 2009
the Mad Hatter hosts the famous gathering in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A US political movement led by a lunatic?
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party is a US political movement, and the Mad Hatter hosts a tea party in Lewis Carroll's story.
